newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kinkel rejects EMU speculation about Italy.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel rejects EMU speculation about Italy.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel dismissed on Saturday speculation about a plan to prevent Italy from being a founder member of a single European currency, one day after Prime Minister Romano Prodi visited Bonn.

Britain's Financial Times reported earlier this week that European Union officials and central bankers were discussing such a plan partly to assuage German fears that the new euro currency would be too soft if southern European nations joined at the start.

Kinkel told German Radio in an interview that there was no such plan, that Germany wanted as many countries as possible to join the economic and monetary union (EMU) and that the only condition to join was to fulfil the Maastricht Treaty criteria.
"It only depends on fulfilment of the (Maastricht) criteria. Italy is doing its best to fulfil these and all this speculation at the moment is wrong," Kinkel told German Radio.
"Only the politicians will decide how we proceed with currency union. Experts can say what they like and they should say what they think, but keeping to the stability criteria is the decisive thing."

Kinkel also echoed Chancellor Helmut Kohl's words, saying that the meeting between Kohl and Italian prime minister Romano Prodi on Friday had been a great success and that there were no problems between Italy and Germany.
